page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.8xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance configuration tailored for compute, memory, and high-speed I/O balance. The instance runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, allocating 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES-NI. System memory totals 128.0 GB of DDR4 clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Unlike diskless general-purpose tiers, the m5dn series incorporates 1200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps. No hardware GPUs are included.

Benchmark results place the m5dn.8xlarge consistently in the middle tier of general compute profiles. The instance scored 26,448.34 on the PassMark CPU test and achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,460.0, backed by a multi-core stress-ng performance of 27,985.53. However, single-threaded processing presents a clear tradeoff: both the stress-ng single-core score of 1,327.69 and single-threaded gzip compression at 22.5 GB/sec rank in the bottom 25%. Memory subsystem throughput remains stable, recording 109.74 GB/sec for uncached 256MB read operations and 48.04 GB/sec for writes. In application-level metrics, Redis SET operations reached 26.47 million operations per second, static web serving delivered 21.47 GB/sec, and small LLM inference registered 1,149.24 prompt tokens per second, though large-model inference degrades to 4.44 tokens per second due to the lack of hardware acceleration.

The hardware composition provides predictable cost efficiency for workloads that concurrently demand significant memory, high network bandwidth, and direct-attached NVMe storage. Because the 1200 GB NVMe SSD volume is integrated directly into the instance profile, the platform circumvents additional network-attached block storage overheads for temporary data and high-frequency scratch space. Workload fits encompass relational and in-memory databases, caching tiers, continuous integration build clusters, static web serving clusters, and distributed data processing pipelines requiring fast local scratch disks.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 1200 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps, with zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation demonstrates consistent mid-tier multithreaded capacity, delivering a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,460.0 and PassMark CPU score of 26,448.34, balanced against lower single-thread throughput. The inclusion of fast local NVMe storage combined with a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio delivers high efficiency for transactional databases, caching layers, CI/CD build environments, and distributed ETL systems needing low-latency local storage.
